scoring_breakdown.font_name: 0.5 - All runs use Times New Roman
scoring_breakdown.italic: 0.5 - At least 90% of text-bearing runs are italic

llm_judge_reasons: Both instruction requirements (font=Times New Roman and all-text italic) are covered by the evaluator with partial credit (0.5 each), matching the instruction exactly.
Metric correctly handles the type='rule' expected parameter: it directly calls expected.get('expected_font', ...) on the rules dict, not expected.get('rules', ...), which is the correct pattern.
Postconfig saves the document with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring file state is current when the getter reads it.
The getter's all_italic threshold of 90% is a practical tolerance that handles edge cases like blank lines or auto-generated formatting runs.

Minor concern: run.font.name only captures explicitly-set run-level font names; runs that inherit font from paragraph/document style have font.name=None and are excluded from font_names. In practice, when a user selects all text via Ctrl+A and changes the font via the toolbar, LibreOffice sets the font explicitly at the run level in the resulting .docx, so this should work correctly.

Minor concern: r.italic is True (strict identity check) only counts runs with explicitly-set italic; inherited italic (None) is not counted. Same practical rationale applies - applying Ctrl+I to selected text sets run-level italic explicitly.

The metric does not use expected_italic from the expected dict (it hardcodes the italic check as all_italic==True). This is semantically correct for this task since expected_italic=True, but would be wrong if expected_italic were False.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider reading effective (inherited) font name using run.font.element or paragraph/document styles as a fallback when run.font.name is None, to handle cases where font is set at paragraph or document style level.

Consider using r.italic or bool(r.italic) instead of r.italic is True to include runs whose italic state is inherited (None can mean inherited italic in some docx contexts), or explicitly document the strict-True-only behavior.
Consider using expected.get('expected_italic', True) in the metric to compare against the expected dict value rather than hardcoding the italic=True check, making the metric more general.
